states.name: Queensland
general_steps: Check what the council's planning scheme says about your project: some work needs no planning approval, some is code assessable and some is impact assessable.
Talk to the council's planning team before you lodge, especially if the project is unusual. Many councils offer pre-lodgement meetings.

Prepare the application: the state's DA Form 1 (DA Form 2 if it includes building work), owner's consent if you don't own the land, plans, and a report showing how the project meets the planning scheme.
Lodge it with the council and pay the application fee.
Answer any information request from the council by the date it gives.
Impact assessable applications are publicly notified before the council decides.
Building work usually also needs a building approval, normally from a private building certifier.

states.name: New South Wales
general_steps: Check what your council's Local Environmental Plan (LEP) allows on your land. Look up the zone on the NSW Planning Portal Spatial Viewer and order a section 10.7 planning certificate for constraints like heritage, bush fire and flooding.

Check whether your work is exempt development (no approval) or can be complying development (a fast-track CDC from council or a registered certifier) under the State codes. If neither fits, you need a development application (DA).
Talk to your council's duty planner, or book a pre-lodgement meeting, if the project is unusual.

Prepare the DA: plans, a statement of environmental effects, a cost estimate, signed owner's consent, and a BASIX certificate for new homes or work over $50,000. Add any specialist reports, such as a bush fire assessment.
Lodge the DA online on the NSW Planning Portal, then pay the fee when council sends the invoice. The assessment clock starts once you pay.
Council notifies neighbours if needed, may ask for more information, then approves the DA with conditions or refuses it. You can ask for a review or appeal.
Before building, get a construction certificate, appoint a principal certifier and give council at least 2 days' notice. Get an occupation certificate before you move in.
